source.title: Module-Aware Parameter-Efficient Machine Unlearning on Transformers
source.authors: Wenjie Bao; Jian Lou; Yu-Ke Hu; Xiaochen Li; Zhi-Hao Liu; Jiaqi Liu; Zhan Qin; Kui Ren

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether relearning fine-tuning can reverse unlearning, using a different method and setup: MAPE-Unlearn and full-parameter updates on TOFU, evaluated by forget quality across relearning epochs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports relearning-attack outcomes in Figure 4. Its other unlearning efficacy and fidelity results do not test the claim versions as a whole: they do not pair near-chance targeted accuracy and preserved general ability with attacks on the same setting. No results are reported for ablation, quantization, or prompting-only recovery. The 20% relearning dataset is not described as unrelated or loosely related.
record.test_reason: Section 5.3 and Figure 4 run a fine-tuning relearning attack on TOFU Forget05 (Llama2-7b-chat). The attack uses a random 20% of samples for 10 epochs, with forget quality tracked per epoch. It compares full-parameter unlearning (bears on B) with the proposed MAPE-Unlearn, which the authors call resistant to relearning (bears on F). No ablation, quantization or prompting attacks are run.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that MAPE-Unlearn shows 'superior robustness compared to full-parameter updates' against relearning. The outcome varies by objective: delayed decline for GA/GD, full defence for NPO, an initial decline for DPO. For DPO, full-parameter updates themselves already defend effectively.
record.recipe_differences: Proposes module-aware sparse updates and evaluates relearning fine-tuning on TOFU; it does not reproduce the original unlearning methods or test the other listed recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with the unlearning objective and parameter-update approach: GA/GD, DPO, and NPO show different relearning outcomes; full updates and 90%-sparse MAPE-Unlearn also differ.

fits_no_version.finding: On WMDP with Zephyr-7B-beta, no attack is run. GA-family unlearning brings WMDP-Bio to about 0.26–0.27 (near 4-choice chance) but cuts MMLU from 0.58 to about 0.40–0.41. NPO keeps MMLU at 0.49 but leaves WMDP-Bio at about 0.45.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning efficacy–utility trade-off on WMDP without any recovery attack (bears on the first half of A only).

record.problems: The relearning outcome is presented in a plot without reported exact values or uncertainty. The attack uses randomly selected 20% of dataset samples, not a stated few unrelated or loosely related examples. Relearning-attack results are reported for one model and one TOFU setting in the main text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relearning-attack results are reported beyond Figure 4. Other unlearning efficacy/fidelity tables and figures were not extracted as claim-version rows because they do not test the corresponding version's full conditions.

untested.parts: No attack is paired with a near-chance, utility-preserving unlearned model. The WMDP results (Table 5) report unlearning without any recovery attack.

Relearning set is a random 20% of samples, not stated to be a small, unrelated or loosely related set, or a defined subset of forgotten facts. Only one model (Llama2-7b-chat) and one split (Forget05) are tested. No WMDP relearning, and no accuracy-based recovery measure.
Not tested: no direction ablation and no blocked-access-versus-deletion analysis.
Not tested: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery.
MAPE-Unlearn is tested only against fine-tuning relearning on TOFU Forget05. There is no test against internal edits, quantization, prompting, or relearning on WMDP.

missing.what: Numeric FQ values per relearning epoch for full and MAPE curves, and whether the relearning 20% is drawn from the forget set or the full TOFU data. Needed to judge recovery magnitude and whether the set counts as 'small'.

record.verdict_notes: Re-linked the MAPE rows (R2, R4, R6, R8) to F only: they measure the counter-method, not recovery in a standard unlearned model. FQ is a KS-test p-value against the retrained model, so a fall in FQ is only an indirect sign of recovered knowledge. The authors tuned hyperparameters to reach reasonable FQ for GA/GD. All relearning evidence is a single figure with no uncertainty, on one model and one split. Original sources are only cited; this study is not one of them.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports unlearning efficacy and fidelity, but does not test whether near-chance targeted performance is retained against simple attacks.

Tests fine-tuning relearning on a randomly selected 20% of dataset samples for up to 10 epochs; does not test a few unrelated or loosely related examples or a subset of forgotten facts as a separate condition.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context-information recovery tests.
Tests MAPE-Unlearn against the reported fine-tuning relearning attack only; does not test resistance to internal edits, quantization, or prompting-only attacks.

relation.reason: Its own relearning-attack results bear on B (full-parameter baselines) and F (MAPE).

tranche.reason: Different method (module-aware sparse updates, FQ under a relearning attack on TOFU) aimed at the same question.

source_check.notes: All relearning results are figure-only (Figure 4, TOFU Forget05, Llama2-7b-chat). The relearning set is a random 20% of 'dataset samples' (split not stated), 10 epochs, lr 1e-5. FQ is a KS-test p-value against the retrained model, so a falling FQ is only an indirect sign of recovery. Authors tuned hyperparameters to get reasonable GA/GD FQ.

statements.correction: This study fixes the attack: a random 20% of dataset samples, 10 epochs, lr 1e-5, batch 16. It varies only the unlearning objective (GA/GD/DPO/NPO) and full vs MAPE sparse unlearning updates. Drop the 2508.17233 R1 citation.
statements.problem: Cites R1 as evidence that the way the attack is run matters, but this study runs only one fixed relearning attack. R1 is full-update GA under that attack and does not bear on attack optimizer, objective or which parameters the attack fine-tunes.

statements.correction: MAPE-NPO, 90% sparsity, TOFU Forget05, Llama2-7b-chat, 10 relearning epochs on a random 20% of dataset samples: authors say it 'successfully defends' while full-parameter NPO fails. Figure-only. Preprint, no code, authors' own test.
statements.problem: R8 does support F, but the statement gives no MAPE result. Its conditions (1B-3B Llama/Qwen, mostly one epoch or a few hundred steps) don't cover this study's Llama2-7b-chat with a 10-epoch attack.

statements.correction: MAPE-DPO, 90% sparsity, TOFU Forget05, Llama2-7b-chat: FQ declines at first, then ends high. Full-parameter DPO 'can effectively defend'. Figure-only. Record verdict: F limits_scope.
statements.problem: The pattern (new method no better than its base) fits R6, but MAPE is not named and the conditions (MUSE, RWKU) don't cover TOFU. MAPE-DPO ends with high FQ, so the record's verdict for R6 is limits_scope (l4), not challenges.

statements.correction: MAPE 'withstand a longer attack duration on GA and GD' than full updates (TOFU Forget05, Llama2-7b-chat, up to 10 relearning epochs; measure: forget quality). Figure-only. Text doesn't say whether FQ later converges.
statements.problem: R2/R4 fit the delay pattern, but MAPE is not named. The text doesn't say FQ converges eventually. The conditions list loss, AUC or extraction strength, but this study measures forget quality (a KS-test p-value).

statements.correction: MAPE at 90% sparsity, TOFU Forget05, Llama2-7b-chat: on GA/GD it withstands a longer attack (a delay); on NPO it defends while full NPO fails; on DPO FQ declines at first, then ends high, while full DPO already defends. Figure-only.
statements.problem: The factor (base method under the counter-method) fits this study, and citing R2, R4, R6 and R8 is apt. But the statement gives none of MAPE's results, so readers can't see what the rows show.
